CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left shoulder pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old female presenting with left shoulder pain that began one week ago. Pain onset occurred during a gymnastics class when patient fell into an awkward position during an exercise. Patient reports severe pain with any movement of the left shoulder, including forward and backward movements. She attempted self-treatment with Tylenol for 2-3 days without relief. X-ray of the left shoulder shows no evidence of fracture or broken bone, suggesting a joint injury. Patient reports prior surgery on the left arm but denies this is related to current symptoms.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports pain with any movement of the left shoulder, specifically with forward and backward movements. No other symptoms documented.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Prior surgery on left arm

MEDICATIONS
Tylenol (used for 2-3 days)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Participates in gymnastics classes

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Shoulder examination reveals pain with forward shoulder movement, pain with backward shoulder movement, and pain with any movement of the left shoulder. X-ray of left shoulder performed.

RESULTS
Left shoulder x-ray: No fracture or broken bone

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left shoulder joint injury. Recommend ibuprofen 600 mg three times daily for one week. If pain persists after one week, consider ice or heat pad application for pain relief. Rest left arm during healing period. Avoid heavy lifting and use right hand for activities for at least 3-4 weeks. Alternative pain medications include Advil or Aleve as needed. Follow up in 3 weeks or sooner if pain persists. May consider repeat x-ray at follow-up if pain does not improve.
